messages:
mia: Quick question — hitting a few customer reports where our Python streaming client turns some API errors into a generic SDK exception and loses the request_id. Behavior looks different if the upstream returns a 502 vs a 4xx with JSON body. Anyone seen this? 

alex: Can you paste a minimal repro or the log lines? Is this during connect or mid-stream? :thinking:

mia: Mid-stream. Customer calls chat.stream() -> after ~3s the connection drops. Our client raises SDKError('service error') with no inner code and no request id. Runtime logs show the upstream returned a JSON error + header: `X-Request-Id: r-12345abc`.

sam: We had a similar case last month — the runtime surfaces error payload in the HTTP body but the SDK only parses headers for request ids on non-stream endpoints. Streaming path uses a framed transport and we swallow the body when framing fails.

leah: Repro logs from customer (sanitized):
```
[2026-02-18T14:22:05Z] client: start stream chat.stream() req=client-867
[2026-02-18T14:22:08Z] upstream: HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
Content-Type: application/json
X-Request-Id: r-12345abc

{"error": {"message": "kv cache mismatch", "code": "KV_CACHE_MISMATCH", "retryable": false}}
[2026-02-18T14:22:08Z] client: raised SDKError('service error') req=client-867
```

leah: Looks like SDK maps anything non-200 during stream to SDKError without extracting `error.code` or X-Request-Id.

alex: Yeah — we should map specific codes -> exceptions (e.g., KVCacheMismatchError, TransientBackendError) and always attach request_id in the exception metadata. That makes debugging and support 100x easier.

mia: Proposed change: in stream error handler, try to parse framing/body as JSON; if JSON has error.code -> pick exception class; also grab X-Request-Id from headers (fallback to body.request_id) and include it on exception and logs. Also add a debug flag to print full raw response.

sam: Two caveats: 1) streaming transport sometimes yields partial frames, so JSON parse can fail — make it defensive. 2) Retries for streaming are tricky: if error is non-idempotent (e.g., KV_CACHE_MISMATCH), do NOT retry; if transient (502 without code), allow reconnect + resume only if resume token exists.

alex: Agree. Suggested pseudo for Python client error mapping: 
```
try:
    body = await read_error_body_safe(resp)  # returns None or dict
except Exception:
    body = None
code = (body or {}).get('error', {}).get('code') if isinstance(body, dict) else None
request_id = resp.headers.get('X-Request-Id') or (body or {}).get('request_id')
if code == 'KV_CACHE_MISMATCH':
    raise KVCacheMismatchError('kv cache mismatch', request_id=request_id)
elif resp.status >= 500:
    raise TransientBackendError('5xx', request_id=request_id)
else:
    raise SDKError('service error', request_id=request_id)
```

leah: Could `read_error_body_safe` limit to first 8k bytes and catch JSONDecodeError? We don't want to block streaming reads.

alex: Yes — also make sure we don't allocate huge buffers. Limit and return None if not parseable. Add unit tests simulating partial frames.

mia: For support: can we update the default debug log format to include request_id if present? E.g. "[ts] client: error ... req_id=r-12345abc code=KV_CACHE_MISMATCH". That will make triage much simpler.

sam: Agreed. For retries: add a clear predicate function `should_retry_stream(error, idempotent)` that checks error type + headers (Retry-After, Retryable in body). If resume token present and idempotent, allow reconnect and resume; otherwise bubble.

ci-bot: ci/build-status: small-patch tests passed (python, node) — 12/12

alex: I'll draft a small PR to implement mapping + request_id propagation and a feature flag `SDK_STREAM_DEBUG=true` for verbose raw-response dumps. Will add unit tests for: header-only request id, body-only request id, partial JSON body.

leah: Awesome. Can you also add a short blurb in SDK docs under "Error handling" showing the new exception classes and example of catching KVCacheMismatchError vs generic SDKError?

mia: Thanks — once PR is up I'll share with the customer (and include the request_id in support ticket). If anyone has objections to the plan, speak now. Otherwise assign to alex. :+1:

sam: No objections. Thanks!

alex: Assigned and starting now. I'll ping here when draft is ready for review.

mia: :rocket:
